coverage_status: Selected scalar rate-coefficient equations only; not the entire kinetics subsystem.

units.rate_coefficients: m, kmol, s to powers determined by reaction order; values must already be converted

equations: k = A exp(bg ln(T) + b ln(Te) - Ea/(RT) + EE(Te-T)/(R Te T) - T/Tinv)
(partial k/partial T)/k at fixed Te = bg/T + (Ea-EE)/(R T^2) - 1/Tinv
branches: Tinv=0 disables the final exponential/derivative term; all six upstream parameters included

equations: kf = sqrt(2 e / me) NA simpson(epsilon F0 sigma, epsilon)
kr = sqrt(2 e / me) NA simpson((epsilon+U) F0 sigma_super, epsilon)
sigma_super grid = [0, energy_i-U] with source cross-section values
branches: Cross sections are endpoint-clamped linear interpolations on the supplied EEDF grid
superelastic rate uses the first tabulated energy as U, matching modifyRateConstants
exclusions: PlasmaPhase EEDF construction/caching, YAML parsing, collision kind inference from species charges, and the native unimplemented temperature derivative

branches: unconfigured evaluation returns NaN
validation rejects an unconfigured rate
exclusions: Native AnyMap construction and intentionally unimplemented serialization

branches: dH <= -4 Ea0 gives zero barrier
dH > 4 Ea0 gives barrier dH
otherwise evaluate full Blowers-Masel expression
exclusions: Reaction stoichiometry and phase partial-molar-enthalpy gathering in updateFromStruct/setContext; caller supplies reaction enthalpy
Derivative includes fixed-enthalpy contribution only, exactly as in the upstream derivative

branches: Troe/Tsang Fcent and all log10(Pr) inputs floor at 1e-300
Troe abs(T3/T1)<1e-300 omits corresponding exponential
Troe T2=0 omits its exponential; nonzero subnormal T2 remains included
SRI c=0 omits exp(-T/c)
SRI defaults d=1,e=0; c,d nonnegative including d=0
Troe/Tsang f1 infinite pole returns F=1
exclusions: Effective third-body concentrations from a full mechanism, efficiencies, shared-state caching, and perturb/restore plumbing
Automatic rate-unit adjustment between conventional and chemically activated reactions

equations: k_i = 1e-300 + sum of Arrhenius terms at pressure i
branches: Multiple terms at identical log-pressure are summed in supplied order
Nearest pressure group is used outside the pressure range
Validation temperatures default to 300,500,1000,2000,5000,10000 K and exclude evaluation floor

equations: log10(k) = sum_i sum_j alpha_ij C_i(Tr) C_j(Pr)
branches: No clamping: extrapolation evaluates the same polynomial outside the fitted limits
exclusions: YAML unit-system offset of coefficient [0][0]; inputs must already be in target units

equations: eps_mix = sum(explicit X_i eps_i) + sum(reference X_i)
k = sum_i(k_i(T,P_eff,i) eps1_i X_i / eps_mix) + k_M(T,P eps_mix) X_M / eps_mix
branches: Reference M efficiency is one
An explicit collider without its own rate uses the reference rate and eps2=1
Troe rates receive P_eff/(R T) as their third-body concentration
exclusions: YAML collider parsing/serialization, phase cache/perturb/restore behavior, and source input-unit conversions

global_exclusions: Full Kinetics, BulkKinetics, InterfaceKinetics, reaction stoichiometry, reverse rates, species production rates, mechanism parsing, unit systems, factories, shared-state caches, serialization, and vectorized MultiRate infrastructure
Surface coverage, sticking, electrochemical, extensible, and vibrational-relaxation rate implementations
Default unconfigured native objects returning NaN are not provided; required parameters are mandatory
C++ exception types and warnings are replaced by Python exceptions and documented derivative semantics
Positive finite T and P and nonnegative M are required; exact overflow/invalid-state IEEE behavior is not promised
tests: tests/test_rates.py: independent algebraic identities, numerical partial derivatives, physical limits, boundaries, duplicate-pressure groups, and polynomial basis expansion; no native dependency. tests/reference_rates.py: optional deterministic randomized comparisons against separately installed native Cantera; prints version, counts, maximum errors, and limitations.
